correctness.rationale: Recomputed all 25 exact ambiguity squares by summing pairs of terms with the cosine of their phase difference, matching the frozen convention and table. The counting-measure squared norm is 5+4t^2. The (0,±1) and (±1,±2) squares meet at the bracketed cubic root t*=0.3784945225024826..., with exact interval bounds placing every other squared ambiguity strictly more than 0.96 above the common value there. The normalized (0,1) branch is strictly increasing from 0 through t*, ruling out 0<=t<t*. For t>t*, the polynomial M(5+4t^2)^2-P_(1,2)(t), with M equal to the squared proposed margin, vanishes at t* and has positive derivative on the nonnegative half-line: its derivative is bounded below by (4/5)t^3-(21/8)t^2+(2/5)t+8, using M>3/40. This proves a strict global comparison with no cutoff on t and yields exactly six active shifts. The independent fixed-parameter value is 0.07274258488949..., versus the optimum 0.27802114614038.... The positive margin meets the published nonvanishing criterion for recovery up to global phase; it is not a full-spark test.
residual_risks: The domain is exactly real t>=0: signed factors 1+t chi(j) for t>1 are part of that domain. No complex-parameter or arbitrary-window optimum is established.
